newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico, U.S. capture hitmen of top drug gang.
newsitem.headline: Mexico, U.S. capture hitmen of top drug gang.

text.p: Mexican and U.S. authorities have captured five alleged hitmen for one of Mexico's most feared drug cartels in a series of raids in Mexico and California, the attorney general said on Wednesday.

Among those taken into custody were two men alleged to have taken part in the mafia-style killing in Mexico City on Sept. 14 of the chief of the anti-drug police in the border state of Baja California, Antonio Lozano Gracia told a news conference.

Garcia said the five were "gatilleros" -- hired guns -- of the Arellano Felix brothers, that reputedly run the Tijuana cartel on the border with the Californian city of San Diego. He catalogued some 18 murders in Mexico that he said the gunmen linked to the three brothers between 1988 and 1996.

Among those arrested were two Arellano Felix gunmen known by the aliases "The Wolf" and "The C.P.", in San Diego California. They were caught by the U.S. Justice Department, following a tip from Mexico, which planned to start extradition proceedings, Lozano Gracia said.
Also, one of the brothers' main hitmen, Fausto Soto Miller, alias "The Chief," was captured by the Mexican army in the central city of Guadalajara.

The attorney general said the authorities were getting nearer to the cartel heads. Evidence of that, he said, was the machine-gunning of Baja California Federal Judicial Police Commander Ernesto Ibarra Santos.
He was shot along with two policemen and a taxi driver near the city centre as he was travelling from Mexico City airport late at night.
"The presumed drug trafficker Ramon Arellano Felix was the one who ordered the execution of the ex-police chief, because he was getting closer to carrying out his arrest," Lozano Gracia said.
But the two men arrested in the killing were not the actual gunmen. They were the driver of one of the gunmen's cars, and a contact who supplied the guns, cars and a safe house, Lozano Gracia said.
